# Design Brief: Locked Landing Direction

**Title**: Sumi-e Drift, rendered as a static asset
**Status**: Implemented (2026-05-10). The shader implementation was superseded by a static asset render of the same composition; see "Decision update" below.
**Register**: brand (this surface only; PRODUCT.md default register is product)
**Generated by**: `/impeccable shape "pick the landing rendition direction from the four variants under app/preview/*"`
**Anchored to**: `PRODUCT.md`, `DESIGN.md`, the four variant components under `components/landing-variants/*` (since pruned)

This brief locks the landing direction for the USM CSS AGM portal. It supersedes the four exploratory variants under `app/preview/*` and the dev-only rendition picker currently shipping at `app/page.tsx`.

---

## Decision update — 2026-05-10: shader → static asset

After three iteration passes inside `/impeccable craft`, the live OGL shader implementation reached only ~85 percent fidelity to the locked north-star mock while still paying a continuous per-frame GPU cost on every device. The team switched to a static-asset rendering of the same composition, generated by an image model, art-directed against the same north-star mock.

**Rationale.** The brief locked *composition* and *perf budget*, not rendering technology. A static asset:

- reaches 100 percent fidelity to the mock instead of the shader's 85 percent approximation;
- collapses the perf question — image decode on first paint is trivial on every device that can render the page at all, which is the brief's hardest criterion (Mali-G52-class budget phones over crowded conference WiFi);
- removes the auth-pause / tab-hidden / DPR-cap scaffolding the shader needed to behave;
- trivially satisfies `prefers-reduced-motion` (no motion to reduce);
- removes WebGL context loss as a failure mode;
- deletes ~250 lines of shader code, three component files, and the `ogl` runtime dependency from the JS bundle.

**Trade-off accepted.** The shader's slow ambient drift (`uTime * 0.025`) is gone. Given the brief's "5 to 10 seconds on AGM day" visit budget, the drift was already near-imperceptible to the actual visitor, so the user-experience cost is negligible.

**Implementation.** `public/landing/sumi-backdrop.png` is the production asset, rendered via `components/landing/landing-backdrop.tsx` as a `next/image` `fill priority` element. The asset is responsive-served (AVIF / WebP per device) by Next.js's image pipeline.

The rest of the brief below still describes the production landing accurately — composition, color story, layout, copy, states, anti-goals, content. Only the rendering technology changed.

---

## 1. Feature Summary

The locked landing direction. **Sumi-e Drift's composition wins** (charcoal smoke in opposite corners, copper calligraphic threads, framed cream centre, serif headline anchor), but its rendering budget is **capped at Whisper Lines's lightness** so the experience holds together on a Redmi-class Android phone over crowded conference WiFi. The lock also sets the loud-surface palette and typography that propagate to `DESIGN.md` as **tokens** (not as motion), so every other surface in the portal inherits the brand identity without inheriting the shader.

## 2. Primary User Action

**Sign in with Microsoft.** The landing has five to ten seconds on AGM day to set the institutional tone, then deliver the visitor to authentication with two pieces of information already absorbed: which AGM cycle this is (the year), and whether they are eligible to sign in at all (the `@student.usm.my` constraint).

## 3. Design Direction

### Composition

**Sumi-e Drift.** Charcoal ink-wash billows concentrated in the top-right and bottom-left corners with lighter wisps in the opposite corners. Long copper calligraphic threads weave through the smoke. A wide rectangular centre clearing keeps the type area calm.

### Color strategy

**Committed** (per loud-surface permission in DESIGN.md). The graphite ink-wash carries 30 to 60 percent of the visible surface; copper accents the threads; cream paper holds the centre. Acid yellow is permitted in micro-doses (Round 2 did not ban it) but only as a small considered accent, not as ambient bloom.

### CTA

The **shared `SignInCTA` component** (Button-in-Button: ink-on-paper pill with paper capsule for arrow icon). Sumi-e variant's custom rectangular Microsoft-branded CTA is **dropped** per Round 2 anti-goals (`no_microsoft_mark`).

### Theme scene sentence

> A second-year USM Computer Science Society committee member opens the portal on AGM day at 14:05 MYT, on a five-year-old Android phone with one bar of conference-hall WiFi, in a packed lecture theatre with overhead fluorescent lighting and other voters peering at their own phones nearby.

This sentence forces **light theme**. Cream paper reads as an institutional document under fluorescent light; dark would read as an app, which is exactly what we are not.

### Anchor references

1. **Sumi-e ink wash** as a classical Eastern visual language. Predates digital design by centuries; doesn't pin to any year. Provides the perceptual ageing strength that won the criterion.
2. **Stripe's signed-in app shells** (calm cream surface, considered typography, no decorative motion) for the institutional restraint register.
3. **The lab-notebook scaffolding** already established in `app/globals.css` and `app/page.tsx` (28 px grid overlay, monospace metadata, technique tags). The grid overlay survives on quiet surfaces; on this loud surface, the shader IS the scaffolding equivalent.

### Typography reflex-reject deferral

The brand register's reflex-reject typography concern (Playfair Display for the serif role) is intentionally **deferred to `/impeccable craft`** per Round 2. The brief locks Sumi-e's structure, composition, and copy direction; the serif itself is decided in the live editor during craft via comparison against non-reflex candidates.

## 4. Scope

| Dimension | Decision |
|---|---|
| Fidelity | **Production-ready**. This is the landing that ships to the `main` branch for AGM 2026. |
| Breadth | **One screen** (`app/page.tsx`), plus the token-propagation pass to `DESIGN.md` and `app/globals.css` that follows the lock. |
| Interactivity | The shader (ambient, paused on tab-hide and on CTA press); the sign-in CTA (initiates Microsoft OAuth). No hover-driven shader interaction (Plexus's cursor-repulsion was not retained). |
| Time intent | **Polish until it ships.** Critical-path surface for AGM 2026. |

## 5. Layout Strategy

Symmetric centered single-viewport. Vertical rhythm:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│        [USM CSS AGM · 2026]   ← brand pill: outlined, solid bg, no glass
│                                             │
│                                             │
│           Elect the next                    │
│           CSS committee.    ← serif headline (font TBD in craft)
│                                             │
│           ┌────────────────────────┐        │
│           │ Sign in with Microsoft → │  ← shared SignInCTA, ink-on-paper
│           └────────────────────────┘        │
│                                             │
│           @STUDENT.USM.MY ACCOUNTS ONLY  ← mono, uppercase, tracking
│                                             │
│                                             │
│                                             │
│  USM Computer Science Society    AGM 2026   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   ↑ TR + BL corners carry the charcoal billows
   ↑ TL + BR carry the lighter wisps
   ↑ Copper threads weave across diagonally
```

### Per-element decisions

- **Brand pill**: top-center, outlined (paper background at ~72 percent opacity, ink border, no blur). Solid surface, **no glassmorphism** (`no_glass_brand_pill` per anti-goals). Includes cycle year inline (`USM CSS AGM · 2026`) so the visitor never has to wonder which year they are looking at.
- **Headline**: large serif, anchored in the rectangular cream centre carved out by the shader. Two lines, deliberate line break.
- **CTA**: shared `SignInCTA`, ink pill with paper capsule for the arrow icon.
- **Eligibility microcopy**: directly under the CTA. Monospace, uppercase, tracking around `0.28em`. Reads as system metadata, not as a footnote.
- **Footer**: bottom edge, society name on the left, AGM cycle year on the right. Drop the rendition attribution that ships in the current variants (the dev artifact is being retired).
- **No grain overlay** (`no_grain_overlay` per anti-goals). One render layer fewer; one "feels designed" tell removed; small perf win.

## 6. Key States

| State | What the visitor sees and feels |
|---|---|
| Default cold load (AGM day, phone, fluorescent light) | Shader active; headline anchors immediately; CTA is the unmistakable focal point; eligibility microcopy answers "can I vote?" before they click. |
| Default desktop / ambient | Same composition; shader more legible; copper threads more apparent. |
| `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` | Shader freezes to a single static frame. Layout, copy, CTA identical. |
| Tab hidden (`document.hidden`) | Shader pauses via the rAF loop's hidden-tab guard. Zero GPU work off-screen. |
| CTA pressed (OAuth redirect in flight) | Shader freezes; CTA enters loading state with spinner; all motion stops during the auth handoff. **Hard rule** (`no_decorative_during_action`). |
| Slow network (shader still loading or WebGL initializing) | Static cream backdrop with headline + CTA visible immediately; shader fades in when canvas is ready. |
| WebGL unavailable (some WebViews, very old devices) | Static fallback: cream paper with subdued ink suggestions in two corners (or pure paper, decided during craft). CTA + headline unchanged. |
| Already-authenticated visitor returning to `/` | Redirect to dashboard (handled by auth provider middleware, not a landing concern). |

## 7. Interaction Model

One interaction: pressing the sign-in CTA. On press:

1. Shader's animation loop pauses (rAF cancelled or guarded by an `auth-in-flight` flag).
2. CTA enters `loading` state (existing behavior in `SignInCTA`: arrow swaps for spinner, label becomes "Signing in").
3. `signInWithRedirect` initiates the Microsoft OAuth flow.
4. On return, the user lands on `/dashboard` (existing user) or `/profile/complete` (first-time user). Out of this brief's scope; the AuthGate handles routing.

**Hover behavior**: desktop only. CTA's arrow capsule slides `0.5` units on hover (existing Button-in-Button pattern). The shader does not respond to cursor; Plexus's repulsion physics are intentionally not carried forward.

## 8. Content Requirements

| Element | Copy | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Brand pill | `USM CSS AGM · 2026` | Mono, uppercase, tracking `0.22em`. Cycle year is canonical identity, not metadata. |
| Headline | `Elect the next` / `CSS committee.` (placeholder, two lines) | **Open question for craft.** Headline is the most visible piece of UX writing in the portal. |
| CTA | `Sign in with Microsoft` (default), `Signing in` (loading) | Existing `SignInCTA` strings. **No 4-colour Microsoft mark visible.** |
| Eligibility microcopy | `@STUDENT.USM.MY ACCOUNTS ONLY` | Mono, uppercase, tracking `0.28em`. Below CTA. |
| Footer left | `USM Computer Science Society` | Mono, uppercase, tracking `0.20em`. |
| Footer right | `AGM 2026` (or full date once published) | Same treatment. Replaces the variant-attribution string. |

The cycle year value (`2026`) should ideally come from a single source of truth (Convex `electionSettings.cycleYear` or a runtime env constant) so next year's committee changes one value, not three.

## 9. Recommended References (for `/impeccable craft`)

- `reference/spatial-design.md` for the symmetric centered single-viewport composition and the principled exceptions (brand pill top-center, footer split bottom).
- `reference/motion-design.md` for shader pause-on-action, reduced-motion handling, and tab-hidden gating.
- `reference/typography.md` plus the brand register reflex-reject list when craft tackles the serif decision.
- `reference/color-and-contrast.md` for the OKLCH-clean propagation of Sumi-e's palette into DESIGN.md (the current shader uses raw RGB triplets like `vec3(0.74, 0.76, 0.79)`; these need conversion to OKLCH-friendly tokens during the lock).
- `reference/optimize.md` after the craft pass, to verify the perf budget on real devices.

## 10. Open Questions (resolved during `/impeccable craft`)

1. **Serif headline font.** Playfair Display is the placeholder; on the brand register reflex-reject list. Resolved live in `/impeccable craft` via comparison against non-reflex serifs (GT Sectra, Editorial New, Authentic Sans, Romie, ABC Sectra are starting candidates). Fallback: drop the serif role entirely and use Unbounded for the headline.
2. **Headline copy.** "Elect the next / CSS committee." is the current placeholder. Worth a focused UX-writing pass during craft against PRODUCT.md voice rules (state the state; specific over vague; never cute, never apologetic).
3. **Acid yellow on the CTA.** Round 2 did not ban the acid right-edge strip but the chosen CTA pattern (shared `SignInCTA`) doesn't currently include acid. Open: gain a small acid moment (focus ring tint, press-state accent, hover capsule highlight) or stay strictly ink-on-paper?
4. **Perf budget targets.** Set explicit numbers before craft begins. Suggested starting points (revisit during the post-craft critique): ≥45 fps on a Snapdragon 6-series device, first paint <100 ms post-hydration, GPU memory ceiling <50 MB, zero continuous shader work when tab is hidden, total CPU <5 percent of one core in steady state.
5. **Static fallback content.** Under reduced-motion or WebGL-unavailable: (a) snapshot of the shader at a chosen moment as WebP, (b) cream paper plus a single ink-border vignette suggestion in two corners, or (c) pure cream paper. Decided during craft.
6. **Token propagation list.** When `/impeccable document` runs after the lock, exactly which tokens propagate beyond the landing? Confirmed: paper, ink, copper, cubic-bezier curve, focus ring teal, the chosen serif role, the existing mono role, the existing display role. **Open**: acid yellow's role across other surfaces.
7. **Brand pill cycle-year format.** `USM CSS AGM · 2026`, `USM CSS AGM 2026`, `USM CSS AGM '26`, or split-line with year as smaller subscript. Open detail for craft.
8. **Dormant waiting state.** Out of scope for this brief but explicitly flagged: the `/vote` dormant state ("no public session active right now") is the next candidate loud surface. Revisit whether a recessed version of the Sumi-e shader applies there when that surface is shaped.

## Appendix A: Comparative scoring that produced the pick

User-weighted criteria (from Round 1): perf on budget phones + ages well across cycles + first-touch power.

| Variant | Perf (lower is better load) | Ages | First-touch | Composite | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sumi-e Drift** | 4 | 5 | 4 | **13** | Best balance across the triad. Wins ageing decisively. |
| Whisper Lines | 5 | 4 | 2 | 11 | Wins perf+ageing. Loses first-touch by design. |
| Particle Plexus | 3 | 3 | 3 | 9 | Middling everywhere. Mouse interaction dead on phones. |
| Marbled Veins | 2 | 2 | 5 | 9 | Strongest first-touch. Worst on the two criteria weighted highest. Emotional mismatch with PRODUCT.md ("elegant brand", not "civic institution"). |

Scores 1 to 5, higher is better. Heuristic synthesis from code-level reads of the variants, not benchmarked output.

The user (Round 2) selected the **Sumi-e + Whisper-Lines-perf hybrid** rather than pure Sumi-e, taking the strongest first-touch+ageing combination but capping the rendering cost at the lightest variant's budget. That hybrid IS this brief.
